episodes.167198: An occluded low drifted eastward from far-northern Wisconsin into the far-western portion of Michigan's Upper Peninsula during the afternoon through early evening of the 1st. Simultaneously, the accompanying warm front stalled in vicinity of the Ohio/Pennsylvania border as a cold front swept eastward across the western two-thirds of Ohio. Isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed along and ahead of the cold front amidst weak to moderate instability and moderate to strong effective bulk shear. There were several reports of hail smaller than penny-size in northeast Ohio, but one report of quarter-size hail was received from Ashtabula County.
episodes.167224: Evening severe thunderstorms developed and produced some large hail.
episodes.167225: A mid afternoon severe thunderstorm developed and produced large hail.
episodes.167279: A frontal boundary and associated mid-upper level shortwave forced a small area of scattered supercell-like convection across the Central Midlands. Deep dry air aloft and sufficient cloud layer shear produced an environment primarily conducive for hail, especially given the isolated storm mode. The scattered convection produced numerous hail reports including multiple significant hail reports up to 2.
episodes.167300: Moisture quickly returned to West Texas during the day on the first ahead of an approaching upper level short wave. In response, scattered thunderstorms rapidly developed late Sunday afternoon. Relatively strong wind shear and moderate instability spurred several of the storms to rotate and produce very large hail. The configuration of the increasing and turning winds with height were right to favor splitting supercell storms. The left splits raced north-northeastward bringing brief heavy rain, large hail, and sporadic wind gusts. Golf ball to baseball size hail fell from the strongest of these northward-racing storms. Western portions of Levelland experienced extensive damage, primarily from shattered glass. The right splits moved slowly to the east, producing locally heavy rains. These storms also dropped huge hail with one greater than baseball size near O'Donnell (Lynn County).
episodes.167423: A thunderstorm that was originally a supercell over southeast Missouri produced a couple reports of severe weather after crossing into southwest Illinois. The storm weakened with loss of daytime heating in the evening. The storm formed earlier in the day immediately ahead of a cold front across southeast Missouri, where lower 60's dewpoints were in place.
episodes.167550: Scattered severe thunderstorms moved across northern Illinois on April 30th producing three tornadoes, large hail, localized wind damage and minor flooding.
episodes.167551: Scattered thunderstorms moved across parts of southern Lake Michigan during the afternoon and evening of April 30th.
episodes.167584: A cold front moving across the Mid-South produced severe thunderstorms causing large hail and damaging wind.
episodes.167585: A cold front moving across the Mid-South produced severe thunderstorms causing large hail and damaging wind.
episodes.167748: A weak upper trough shifted southeast from Western Iowa and Eastern Nebraska into Oklahoma and Arkansas during the afternoon and evening of April 30th, reinforcing a weak cold front southeast into Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and North Louisiana during the evening through the early morning hours of May 1st. A warm, moist, and unstable air mass was in place ahead of the front, with increasing large scale forcing along and ahead of the front and approaching trough resulting in scattered shower and thunderstorm development over portions of Southwest Arkansas and North Louisiana. An isolated severe thunderstorm developed over Southern Union County Arkansas, which produced large hail several miles south of El Dorado before weakening during the late evening hours.
episodes.167749: A weak upper trough shifted southeast from Western Iowa and Eastern Nebraska into Oklahoma and Arkansas during the afternoon and evening of April 30th, reinforcing a weak cold front southeast into Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and North Louisiana during the evening through the early morning hours of May 1st. A warm, moist, and unstable air mass was in place ahead of the front, with increasing large scale forcing along and ahead of the front and approaching trough resulting in scattered shower and thunderstorm development over portions of Southwest Arkansas and North Louisiana. An isolated severe thunderstorm developed over Northeast Lincoln and Southwest Union Parishes in North-central Louisiana, where damaging winds downed a tree several miles northwest of Downsville along the Lincoln/Union Parish line. These storms weakened and moved out of the region during the early morning hours of May 1st.
episodes.167877: A cold front brought a broken line of thunderstorms to the state during the afternoon and evening hours of April 30th. One storm tracked from southwest White County east southeastward toward the Mississippi River. It produced hail and even a brief tornado near Des Arc (Prairie County) just before 6 PM CST. A separate storm produced hail briefly along with a weak tornado near Tull (Grant County).
episodes.167947: Afternoon thunderstorms produce wind damage to a few structures in Highlands County.
episodes.168103: A strong cold front pushed across the region Sunday afternoon and evening producing thunderstorm wind damage and large hail. Increased southerly flow and warm air advection helped push temperatures into upper 70s and low 80s with dewpoints in the 60s adding support for scattered shower and storm activity. Instabilities, mid -level lapse rates, and deep layer shear values were modest with MLCAPE  (Mixed Layer Convective Available Potential Energy) near 1,000 j/kg, mid-level lapse rates of 6-8 degrees C per km, and 0-6 km bulk effect shear values around 40-50 kts.
episodes.168115: A strong cold front pushed across the lower Virginia Piedmont Sunday afternoon and evening producing large hail and thunderstorm wind damage. Increased southerly flow and warm air advection helped push temperatures into upper 70s and low 80s with dewpoints in the 60s adding support for scattered shower and storm activity. Instabilities, mid -level lapse rates, and deep layer shear values were modest with MLCAPE (Mixed Layer Convective Available Potential Energy) near 1,000 j/kg, mid-level lapse rates of 6-8 degrees C per km, and 0-6 km bulk effect shear values around 40-50 kts.
episodes.168216: Rainfall persisted across the area between April 28th and May 1st with three day totals over 3 inches between Edmunds, McPherson and Brown counties as well as upstream in North Dakota. This, combined with planned releases due to construction on the Elm Lake Spillway, resulted in minor flooding along the Elm River. Flooding was already occurring during the morning of May 1st and continued into May 2nd with a crest of 13.95 feet at the gauge near Frederick. The gauge at Westport went into flood stage on May 2nd, peaked in stage at 14.4 feet around mid day on May 4th, and then rapidly fell below flood stage on the morning of May 5th.
episodes.168217: River flooding due to snowmelt and excess moisture was already ongoing along portions of the James at the start of the month and did not abate. The James River at Columbia crested at 18.32 feet on May 20 and has been in flood stage the whole month, though impacts are limited to agricultural lands.||Total flood costs related to agriculture land were obtained from the USDA Cause of Loss Summary of Business report.
episodes.168521: Thunderstorms developed along a cold front as it moved into a warm, moist airmass. Some of these storms produced large hail.
episodes.168561: A cold front triggered a line of strong to severe thunderstorms across central Illinois during the late afternoon and evening of April 30th.  One of the storms spawned a brief rain-wrapped tornado in rural McLean County southwest of Colfax.  No damage was reported.  Other storms along the line produced hail as large as half dollars and a few damaging wind gusts.  The storms primarily impacted locations from the I-55 corridor eastward to I-57 before weakening as they tracked further east later in the evening.
episodes.168681: A strong upper level low pressure system moved across Nevada and Utah. Very moist air was across most of West Texas and Southeast New Mexico. High instability and wind shear were also present. An upper level disturbance had moved over the area which provided additional lift. During the afternoon and evening hours, numerous severe thunderstorms developed across Southeast New Mexico and the Trans Pecos and moved across the Stockton Plateau and the Permian Basin. These storms produced multiple tornadoes, very large hail, heavy rainfall leading to localized flooding, and damaging winds.
episodes.168683: A strong upper level low pressure system moved across Nevada and Utah. Very moist air was across most of West Texas and Southeast New Mexico. High instability and wind shear were also present. An upper level disturbance had moved over the area which provided additional lift. During the afternoon and evening hours, numerous severe thunderstorms developed across Southeast New Mexico and the Trans Pecos and moved across the Stockton Plateau and the Permian Basin. These storms produced large hail across Southeast New Mexico.
episodes.168796: Water held back from the Elm Lake Spillway was released, causing minor flooding along the Elm River near Frederick. The flooding, which continued into May, impacted agricultural lands along the river.
episodes.168841: A cold front moving through our southeastern counties generated strong and severe storms that produced severe-criteria hail.
episodes.168896: A diffuse frontal system along with moist east winds and cold air aloft contributed to the development of showers and strong thunderstorms over the local Atlantic waters.
episodes.169012: Isolated thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours in the vicinity of a surface trough. One thunderstorm in Screven County produced an isolated hail report.
episodes.169162: As a cold front moved into the region, some storms occurred in association with this front. Hail was the main concern.
episodes.169226: A brief gustnado appears to have formed near the edge of a strong shower, causing minor damage.
episodes.169252: Clusters of thunderstorms moved through central Kentucky during the pre-dawn hours on May 1st in association with a cold front passing through the region.
episodes.169310: Strong thunderstorms developed across northwest Florida and produced large hail.
episodes.169417: A weak frontal zone sat and wavered generally west to east across North Carolina. A mid level perturbation along with daytime heating spawned loosely organized thunderstorms, starting in the Triad region around in the mid to late afternoon and growing upscale and expanding across the Piedmont with an east-southeastward motion. Some of the strongest storms became severe and produced damaging wind gusts and large hail. Storms became outflow dominant and weakened as they headed into eastern portions of central North Carolina.
episodes.169501: Severe thunderstorms developed across the eastern plains late in the day and into the evening time frame. These storms were isolated and remained in Bent and Prowers Counties, with large hail and wind gusts up to around 65 MPH occurring with the strongest storms.
episodes.169590: A male and female, both 74 years old, from Arcadia, Oklahoma attempted to pass through a low water crossing on the Cannonball River near 96th Ave. SW and 71st St. SW in Hettinger County at around 1:00 PM MDT on May 1. They had crossed successfully at the same location twice the day before. This crossing is locally known to have water running through it during most snowmelt and rain events. A gauge upstream near Regent showed that the river rose approximately two feet on April 30, though still well below flood stage, so no flood warning was in effect. At the time of the attempted crossing, the water was approximately three to four feet deep over the low water crossing. Their vehicle, a 2017 Ford F-250, lost traction and went into the river. The couple placed a call to 911 after they lost control of the vehicle. The vehicle was recovered 1,600 feet to the east of the crossing, with both occupants deceased inside.
episodes.169696: The combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles saw an influx of moisture from the Gulf of Mexico on May 1st. This axis of low level moisture followed the Rio Grande before moving north up over west Texas. This created an unstable environment primed for severe thunderstorms from the Midland/Odessa area up through the Texas and Oklahoma Panhandles. Thunderstorms initiated along the New Mexico/Texas state line and moved east to northeast depending on the nature of the storm. Multiple supercells formed in the late afternoon into evening hours. These supercells had plenty of moisture, instability and increasing winds with height that enabled them to become severe with very large hail and damaging winds which exceeded 80 mph in some cases.
episodes.169926: Isolated thunderstorms developed across the North Carolina foothills during the afternoon. A couple of the storms produced large hail.
episodes.169927: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the South Carolina Piedmont during the afternoon. A couple of storms produced brief large hail in York County.
episodes.170031: A frontal boundary was stalled across northern Louisiana and Mississippi. As a meso-scale convective system developed along this boundary, it began racing southeast towards the Gulf of Mexico. Although the majority of the storms within this system were sub-severe, one portion of the leading edge intensified to produce strong thunderstorm winds over Lake Borne.
episodes.170071: A cold front driven by gusty outflow winds moved through northern Utah, with a redevelopment of high winds behind the initial line across the West Desert.
episodes.170127: Heavy rains brought river flooding to portions of the Ouachita, Black, Spring, White, and Cache Rivers.
episodes.170168: An early May cold front moved into the area and produce a round of thunderstorms across the region. Some storms became severe.
episodes.170177: An inverted surface trough, deep tropical moisture, and an upper-level trough led to the development of strong to severe thunderstorms over north-central Puerto Rico during the afternoon hours of May 1st, 2022. Urban flooding and an EF-1 tornado were observed with the thunderstorms.

A thunderstorm produced a tornado in Pecos County approximately 19 miles north northwest of Fort Stockton. This tornado was seen and reported by a spotter. This tornado was difficult to photograph as it quickly became rain-wrapped and eventually dissipated as the storm approached State Highway 18 in northern Pecos County. This tornado was estimated to have lasted around 12 minutes and traveled southeast approximately 4.5 miles. These calculations were determined from both radar data and eyewitness reports on the ground. Due to the rural location of this tornado, access to any damage indicators was impossible and thus the tornado was rated EF-Unknown with unknown peak wind speeds. The path width of the tornado is unknown.

Given the proximity to the highway, many storm spotters were able to identify and photograph this tornado. Based upon eyewitness reports, videos, and radar data, this tornado tracked northeastward for two and a half miles and was estimated to have lasted around ten minutes. Due to the rural nature of this tornado and lack of access to damage indicators, this tornado was rated EF-Unknown with unknown peak wind speeds. The path width is also unknown.
